title: Generate–Verify–Repair for Intent-Driven Network Changes: Controlled Evaluation with a Deterministic Verifier
abstract: We test whether a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline—single-shot LLM generation followed by a deterministic network verifier and up to one automated repair attempt—reduces accepted unsafe network changes relative to LLM-only generation. In a preregistered paired design (N=500 intents; shared single initial candidate per intent) we used gpt-5-mini for generation and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the adjudicating oracle. Outcomes: guarded (GVR) accepted 500/500 final changes; baseline (LLM-only) accepted 496/500 (paired difference = 0.008). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 0.125; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) = [0.002, 0.016]. Repairs were invoked only when the shared initial candidate failed verification: 4 repair calls total; total model calls = 504 (500 initial + 4 repair). The numerical improvement for GVR is small and does not meet the preregistered per-test significance threshold after the planned multiplicity adjustments; additionally, the preregistered templated-automation comparator was not executed in this archived run and therefore the original two-test Bonferroni plan could not be fully applied. We (1) clarify the shared-initial protocol and execution accounting, (2) give a concise verifier specification and known blind spots, (3) present the confirmatory statistics and reconciliation with archived artifacts, and (4) summarize operational implications and limitations.

sections.introduction: Automation that translates operator intent into device configuration promises efficiency but raises operational risk when generated changes are incorrect, out of sequence, or violate policy. Prior work documents active interest in LLMs for intent-driven NetOps and emphasizes hallucination, sequencing errors, and policy violations as central reliability concerns. Deterministic configuration verifiers can detect many classes of correctness violations before deployment; combining generation with verification and automated repair (generate–verify–repair, GVR) is an intuitive safeguard. We preregistered and executed a paired experiment to answer: Does a GVR pipeline (LLM → deterministic verifier → one automated repair attempt) produce fewer accepted unsafe changes than LLM-only generation on a standardized synthetic NetOps intent workload? Our contributions are: (i) a preregistered paired experiment (N=500) executed end-to-end with archived artifacts; (ii) a concise, artifact-grounded description of the shared-initial generation protocol and deterministic verifier role; and (iii) transparent confirmatory statistics, reconciled execution accounting, and a clear statement of limitations, including an unexecuted preregistered comparator.
sections.related_work: Surveys and recent systems papers document LLM applications in NetOps (intent translation, AIOps, multi-agent orchestration) and recommend tool-augmentation (verifiers, simulators, constraint checkers) to mitigate hallucination and factual errors. Deterministic and formal configuration-verification tools (e.g., Batfish-derived verifiers and incremental checkers) are commonly used to assert reachability and policy constraints before pushing changes. Prior evaluations tend to be heterogeneous in scope and rarely take the form of preregistered, paired trials that run identical generator outputs under both guarded and unguarded conditions; this gap motivated our controlled paired design.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and experimental design: The study was preregistered (study-hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-29) and specified a paired binary estimand: per-intent success difference (guarded − baseline). Sampling: 500 distinct synthetic intents stratified across topology profiles and difficulty levels. Model and pipeline: generation used gpt-5-mini. To ensure strict pairing, each intent produced a single shared initial candidate via the LLM (shared_initial_generation). Baseline (LLM-only) accepted that candidate as the final change; guarded (GVR) first applied deterministic_netops_validator_v5 to the same candidate and, if the verifier failed, invoked up to one automated repair attempt (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). The verifier’s binary decision is the final adjudication for success/failure. Analysis: the preregistered confirmatory test was an exact McNemar two-sided test on discordant pairs plus paired bootstrap percentile 95% CIs (10,000 resamples; bootstrap seed = 1729). Multiplicity: the preregistration planned two confirmatory comparisons with a family α = 0.05 (Bonferroni per-test α = 0.025); because the templated-automation comparator was not executed, that two-test familywise plan could not be fully applied—we report and interpret the executed comparison accordingly and mark the unexecuted arm as unresolved.
sections.results: Execution accounting and reconstruction: completed_episode_count = 1000 (500 intents × 2 condition-episodes), model_calls_used = 504 (500 shared initial generations + 4 repair calls). Repair calls were invoked for exactly those shared initial candidates that failed the verifier. Contingency table of paired outcomes (N=500 pairs): n11 = 496 (both succeed), n10 = 4 (guarded succeed, baseline fail), n01 = 0 (baseline succeed, guarded fail), n00 = 0 (both fail). Thus baseline_success_rate = 496/500 = 0.992; guarded_success_rate = 500/500 = 1.000; paired_difference = 0.008. Confirmatory inference: exact McNemar two-sided p = 0.125 (discordant total n = 4; all in direction guarded>baseline). Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) for the paired difference = [0.002, 0.016]. Interpretation of inference: the bootstrap CI excludes zero by a small margin while the exact McNemar p-value is > the preregistered per-test α (0.025) because exact conditional tests are conservative with small discordant counts and asymmetric directionality (here n=4, k=4). Under the preregistered multiplicity plan (which required two confirmatory tests), the observed p does not meet the adjusted threshold; moreover, because the templated-automation arm was not executed, the originally planned Bonferroni adjustment could not be fully applied—readers should therefore treat significance claims conservatively. Cost diagnostics: repairs invoked = 4; total model calls = 504; mean model calls per accepted change ≈ 1.008; median repair iterations under GVR = 0. Reconciliation and reproducibility: all primary counts and statistics above reconcile with the archived analysis artifacts (paired contingency and condition summaries) and the execution manifest.
sections.discussion: What the numbers mean operationally: in this controlled synthetic workload the GVR pipeline corrected four verifier-detectable unsafe initial candidates that would have been accepted by an unguided LLM-only workflow, at minimal model-call overhead. The absolute improvement (0.8 percentage points) is small relative to the preregistered target effect (≈8 percentage points used in power planning), so the experiment was not powered to treat such a small effect as definitive. Threats to validity: (1) Construct validity—‘safe’ is defined with respect to deterministic_netops_validator_v5’s encoded checks (see below); passing the verifier is necessary for the experiment’s success metric but not necessarily sufficient for all real-world safety properties. (2) External validity—tasks and topologies are synthetic; vendor-specific CLIs, production telemetry, and live-device side effects were not evaluated. (3) Model scope—only gpt-5-mini was evaluated. (4) Unexecuted comparator—the preregistered templated-automation arm was not executed; therefore the original multiplicity correction plan could not be fully applied and the familywise error interpretation is partial. Verifier specification (concise): deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces the following rule categories on candidate configurations: syntactic parsing and normalization (command-level parsing, canonical ordering), required-sequence/workflow-policy checks (e.g., enforced 'must_be_down_for_fields' and ordered shutdown/restore patterns), protected-interface rules (do not modify specified management or protected interfaces), group and availability constraints (minimum/maximum active interfaces in an interface group, make-before-break sequence patterns), dependency-rule enforcement (field-level dependencies such as paired MTU changes requiring synchronized steps), and final-state comparison against the task’s expected_final_state. The verifier returns a non-empty violation set for any failed rule; any non-empty violation set yields a failing verdict for the experiment’s binary outcome. Known blind spots: the verifier encodes a finite rule set and relies on the task payload’s expected_final_state and explicit workflow policies; it does not model device-specific idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane convergence timing, or latent side-effects observable only on live hardware. The artifact bundle contains validator traces and scoring records for each episode; the full validator implementation, ruleset, and code-level mapping of violation codes are archived with the run. (The archived bundle contains the detailed validator artifacts; a human-readable codebook of violation-code strings and precise implementation logic is available in the archived validator materials; that mapping is not reproduced verbatim in this paper.) Practical implication: deterministic verification plus a short automated repair loop can eliminate verifier-detectable unsafe generator outputs with low overhead in a synthetic setting, but production adoption requires broader verifier coverage, multi-model evaluation, adversarial robustness testing, and execution of the planned templated comparator.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered paired experiment (N=500) comparing a generate–verify–repair pipeline (gpt-5-mini + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + up to one automated repair) to LLM-only generation found a small numerical advantage for GVR (500 vs 496 accepted safe changes; paired difference = 0.008; 95% bootstrap CI [0.002, 0.016]; exact McNemar two-sided p = 0.125). Repairs were invoked only when the shared initial candidate failed verification (4 repair calls total); total model calls = 504. The observed improvement does not meet the preregistered adjusted significance threshold and must be interpreted in light of verifier coverage limitations and the unexecuted templated-automation comparator. We recommend replication across multiple LLMs, expanded/verifier coverage, targeted adversarial NetOps evaluations, and execution of the preregistered templated comparator before asserting broader operational readiness. Key artifacts (raw results, paired contingency, condition summaries, execution manifest, and analysis logs) are archived in the evidence bundle for reproducibility.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an explicit autonomy lock. Generation model used in the archived run: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 using the hosted provider recorded as 'openai_responses'. Key automated components recorded in the run: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (task synthesis), deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (primary deterministic verifier/scorer), and the GVR controller implementing shared_initial_generation plus an automated single-repair step (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). The study design, preregistration, code generation, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and revision were performed autonomously after the autonomy lock; no human manually edited or rewrote manuscript technical content after that lock. The preregistered study identifier is study-hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-29. The immutable initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The execution completed according to the archived manifest; key high-level execution quantities reported in this paper (N=500 complete pairs; model_calls_used=504; repair calls=4; paired counts n11=496, n10=4, n01=0, n00=0) are derived from the archived execution and analysis artifacts. The preregistered templated-automation comparator was not executed in this archived run; that unexecuted arm means the originally preregistered two-test Bonferroni familywise plan could not be fully applied and readers should interpret multiplicity-adjusted claims accordingly. Full raw artifacts, logs, and reconciliations are archived in the evidence bundle (execution raw results, analysis contingency and summaries, and execution manifest) for independent verification.
limitations: Synthetic tasks and topology profiles were used (synthetic_topologies_v1 and synthetic_device_configs_v1); external validity to production hardware, vendor-specific CLIs, and live telemetry is untested.
Only a single generation model (gpt-5-mini) was evaluated; multi-model generality is not established.

Safety is defined relative to deterministic_netops_validator_v5’s encoded rule set: syntactic parsing/normalization, required-sequence/workflow-policy checks (must_be_down_for_fields, ordered shutdown/restore patterns), protected-interface rules, group and availability constraints, dependency-rule enforcement, and final-state comparison to the task's expected_final_state. Passing the verifier is necessary for the experiment’s outcome but not sufficient for all real-world safety properties.

The detailed code-level mapping from violation-code identifiers to human-readable descriptions is contained in the archived validator artifacts but is not reproduced verbatim in this paper; this omission is an explicit limitation of the manuscript and the archived validator materials should be consulted for the precise codebook.

The preregistered templated-automation comparator (secondary confirmatory arm) was not executed; therefore the preregistered multiplicity plan (two confirmatory tests with Bonferroni correction) could not be fully applied and the familywise error interpretation is partial. Replication with the templated arm executed is required to complete the preregistered confirmatory plan.
